Juanita Euka (voice) David Pattman (percussion & voice) David Rahman (percussion & voice) Gaspar Sena (percussion & voice) Keryl Brown (percussion & voice) Vicky Jassey (percussion & voice)
Rumba is a secular Afro-Cuban musical tradition that emerged in Cuba from a rich blend of African-derived and Spanish musical influences. Rooted in community and celebration, it brings together percussion, song and dance and has traditionally flourished in homes, courtyards and neighbourhood gatherings.
Drawing on these traditions, La Polémica brings a distinctly British voice to Cuban folkloric music, bringing together some of the UK’s leading percussionists and specialists in Afro-Cuban music.
At the heart of the music are the interlocking rhythms of congas, cajon and other percussion, alongside call-and-response singing and the dynamic relationship between rhythm, song and dance. La Polémica draws on different Afro-Cuban musical traditions and rumba styles while bringing together the individual voices, experiences and influences of its UK-based musicians.
Energetic, rhythmic and deeply communal, La Polémica celebrates rumba as a living tradition: music that brings people together, invites participation and continues to evolve wherever it is played.

 

Friday 27th November, 2:30pm-4:30pm

Clothworkers Centenary Concert Hall

Afro Cuban Rumba Workshop

Following their lunchtime concert, La Polémica lead a practical workshop on Afro Cuban Rumba. Attendees can participate in one of three concurrent sessions as percussionists (congas, clave and shekere will be provided), singers or dancers. The workshop will conclude with the groups coming together for a vibrant performance.
Free to attend - booking not required.
